analysis.title: US Telecom: Implications from Starlink's Q3 results - from broadband threat to wireless question
key_insights: SpaceX's Q3 Connectivity segment revenue grew 69% YoY and EBITDA grew 82% YoY. EBITDA margin was 67%, up from 61% in Q2, which implies expanding operating leverage.
Connectivity revenue and EBITDA exceeded consensus by 7% and 16%, continuing a pattern of upside surprises.
Connectivity subscribers reached 13.6M against 14.2M expected, after a small Q2 miss (12M vs 12.2M expected). Sequential subscriber growth slowed to 13% from 17% in the prior quarter.
Bernstein's takeaway is that Starlink's economics are improving faster than its subscriber base.

Slowing subscriber growth suggests Starlink is not yet taking share aggressively enough to materially change the competitive landscape for FWA or cable broadband operators. Near-term implications for incumbents remain limited.

Rising ARPU ($69/month), expanding margins and continued capacity expansion change the long-term setup. Starlink is becoming profitable before the V3 satellite capacity step-up, which lets it consider aggressive pricing to compete for share.

Bernstein believes the question is not whether Starlink competes on price but when. Capacity is the gating factor and is gradually being addressed. SpaceX may compete aggressively to seed share before fully deploying the V3 constellation.
Starlink Mobile is the bigger concern than Starlink broadband. SpaceX has committed roughly $30B to wireless assets between Echostar and Grain spectrum, and the route to market is unclear.

Building a fourth carrier takes years, so near-term impact is unlikely. The anticipation alone is likely to remain an overhang on US telecom stocks, particularly as the industry approaches the next C-band auction.
Bernstein maintains Market-Perform ratings on AT&T (PT $24), Verizon (PT $45), T-Mobile (PT $180), Comcast (PT $23) and Charter (PT $120), all unchanged.

earnings_insights: SpaceX Q3 (reported, call pulled forward) Connectivity segment revenue +69% YoY and EBITDA +82% YoY. EBITDA margin was 67% vs 61% in Q2.
SpaceX Q3 Connectivity revenue beat consensus by 7% and EBITDA beat consensus by 16%.
SpaceX Q3 Connectivity subscribers reported at 13.6M vs 14.2M consensus expected. Q2 was 12M vs 12.2M expected. Sequential subscriber growth was 13% vs 17% in the prior quarter.
risk_factors: Starlink could price aggressively to seed share before fully deploying V3 satellites, pressuring FWA and cable broadband.
Starlink Mobile and SpaceX's roughly $30B commitment to wireless spectrum create a long-dated overhang for US wireless carriers.
The next C-band auction could intensify the overhang.
AT&T upside risk: a delay in SPCX's wireless entry or in Starlink V3 deployment.

tension_points.bull_case: Starlink broadband subscriber growth is slower than feared (13.6M vs 14.2M expected, 13% sequential vs 17%), so incumbent FWA and cable broadband face limited near-term share loss.
tension_points.bear_case: Starlink's economics are improving faster than its subscriber base (67% margin, $69 ARPU), leaving room to price aggressively before V3 satellites arrive. Starlink Mobile with about $30B in wireless assets is a long-term overhang.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Starlink choosing to compete aggressively on price to seed share before fully deploying V3, or a credible route to market for Starlink Mobile ahead of the next C-band auction.

theme_stances.key_argument: Starlink's economics are improving faster than its subscriber base, and Starlink Mobile remains a long-term overhang for US telecom.
